children: Brazil's central bank chief Gabriel Galipolo said on Monday that the purchasing power of the minimum wage has risen significantly in recent years, but acknowledged that the gains have also "undoubtedly" added to inflationary pressures.

Speaking at an event hosted by lender Itau, he also said that some public expenditures linked to revenue growth create feedback mechanisms that fuel inflation. Galipolo argued that it is possible to preserve social programs and benefits while revisiting rules that could lead to a more "harmonious" mix of economic policies.

title: Brazil's Galipolo says rising minimum wage pressures inflation, calls for policy recalibration
